SPORTS MEDICINE

Knee instability after a sports injury: understanding ACL care

From a twisting injury to a return-to-activity plan, explore the key decisions in ACL injury care.

Explore the steps ↓

A considered plan begins with listening and is shaped around the patient’s symptoms, examination and goals.

01

Recognising the injury

A sudden twist or landing can be followed by swelling, pain or a feeling that the knee gives way. These symptoms have several possible causes, so a clinical assessment is important rather than assuming an ACL tear.

02

Examining the knee

The doctor asks how the injury happened, checks movement and stability and looks for signs of other injury. X-rays may be used to assess bone; MRI can help assess ligaments, meniscus and other soft tissues when appropriate.

03

Discussing treatment choices

The plan depends on instability, other injuries, health and activity goals. Physiotherapy may help restore movement and strength. For some patients, particularly when instability or associated injuries affect their goals, arthroscopic ACL reconstruction may be discussed.

04

Rehabilitation and return to activity

A structured rehabilitation programme works on swelling, range of motion, strength, balance and control. Return to running or sport is guided by progress and clinical assessment; timelines vary with the injury and individual.

FOR YOUR CONSULTATION

Questions to ask

Are other structures injured? Can rehabilitation meet my goals? What milestones should I reach before returning to sport?
